chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar quoted Al-Abbas ibn Ma’ruf, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Sayrafi, on the authority of Hammad ibn Uthman that he told Aba Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'Various narrations come to us from you.'
He (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, the Quran was revealed in seven letters (ahruf), and the least that is permissible for an Imam is to issue decrees in seven different ways (wujuh).'
'This is Our bounty; bestow it or withhold it without account.'
And he (peace be upon him) added: 'This is Our bounty; whether thou bestow them (on others) or withhold them, no account will be asked.'

key_terms.أَحْرُفٍ: Seven modes or letters of Quranic revelation, allowing for variations in recitation and meaning.
key_terms.إِمَامٍ: The Divine Leader or Imam, possessing the authority to issue decrees.
key_terms.عَطَاؤُنَا: Our bounty or gift, referring to the flexibility granted by God in religious law.
key_terms.وَجْهٍ: A way, perspective, or facet; here referring to different legal interpretations or rulings.

ai.seo_question: What is the basis for differing legal opinions in Shia Islam according to the concept of seven ahruf?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* establishes the theological foundation for *ikhtilaf al-fuqaha* (diversity of jurists) by drawing a parallel between the Quran’s seven *ahruf* and the Imam’s capacity for multiple legal interpretations. It underscores that this jurisprudential flexibility is not a defect but a deliberate divine mercy, allowing the Imam to tailor rulings to varying contexts and needs. The citation of Surah Sad 38:88 highlights the Imam’s authority to grant or withhold these interpretive benefits without strict accounting, emphasizing the benevolent nature of this pluralism.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 7-44 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Saffar quoted Al-Abbas ibn Ma’ruf, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Sayrafi, on the authority of Hammad ibn Uthman that he told Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB), “‘We have received various narrations on the authority of the Divine Leaders.’
He (MGB) said, ‘The Quran was revealed in seven letters. The least allowed thing for a Divine Leader is to issue decrees in seven different ways.’
Then as-Sadiq (MGB) added, ‘Such are Our Bounties: whether thou bestow them (on others) or withhold them, no account will be asked.’”
